case_title: Uttam Chakraborty v. State of Assam
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder, death sentence for one accused, life imprisonment for the other
neutral_facts: The accused-husband and his friend were friends. The accused-husband was married to a woman who was pregnant. The couple had a child who was about 4 or 5 years old. The deceased was employed as a school teacher and had engaged a domestic help who resided in their house. The prosecution alleged that the accused-husband and the domestic help had an illicit relationship, which led to frequent quarrels between the couple. On the night of the incident, the domestic help's mother was informed that her daughter had fallen ill and accompanied them to the police station. There, she learned that her daughter had died of burn injuries and lodged a FIR. During the investigation, it was found that the accused-husband was present when the deceased died. The prosecution relied primarily on the testimony of the child witness and the domestic help, as well as the post-mortem report indicating severe injuries and the removal of the foetus.
